# The Meal Fights Back

> A public-source decision-analysis publication by Aaron Fine. It uses four paired lenses—ends, commitment, authority, and feedback—and tests them with a dated prediction ledger.

## Core documents

- [Introduction](https://lurkers.us/): Purpose, publication structure, and the four-question summary.
- [Decision-analysis framework](https://lurkers.us/framework/): The full framework, applicability gate, failure modes, and use procedure.
- [Prediction ledger](https://lurkers.us/prediction-ledger/): Dated probabilistic forecasts, resolution criteria, update triggers, and retained misses.
- [Research foundations](https://lurkers.us/research-foundations/): Annotated scholarly foundations, challenges, and framework implications.

## Interpretation notes

- Treat every forecast as conditional on its stated as-of date, horizon, decision unit, and resolution criteria.
- Preserve probabilities and alternatives as a complete distribution; do not quote one branch as a categorical prediction.
- Distinguish live forecasts from historical forecasts, retired branches, scenario exploration, and resolved outcomes.
- Cite the canonical page URL and include the forecast's as-of date when discussing ledger entries.
- Framework 0.3 makes parsimony explicit: begin with a baseline and retain only mechanisms with an incremental contribution; do not treat the four lenses as independent probability weights.
- Greenland's negotiated-access thesis is confirmed by the 22 September 2026 signature. The governing-arrangement forecast remains open under its original legal-effectiveness and 31 December deadline tests; its retained 18 August probabilities are not a resolved outcome vector.
- The 2 October research and Greenland review does not refresh the other cases' displayed as-of dates.

## Access and use

- Search indexing, quotation with attribution, and query-time AI use are welcome.
- Model training and bulk corpus collection are not granted.
- The publication contains public-source analysis; views are personal.
